messages.subject: Regime dependent IRFs from TVARs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mat and everyone.
I am new to the R software.
I'm currently exploring the possibility of tracking asymmetries in the propagation of shocks to a structural relation(SVAR) without necessarily reporting the parameter estimates. Specifically my thesis is about documenting the varied responses of monetary policy options via the transmission mechanism when the economy is plagued by excess liquidity( a sort of external threshold variable) in the financial system. I reckon a TVAR, with regime dependent impulse response functions will suffice.

The codes for running the TVAR seem very explicit(THANKS for developing them), however, i would also need a clear guide and the codes to run the corresponding regime dependent impulse response functions from the TVAR analysis.

Thanks a lot and have a splendid day.
Waiting on your reply.

messages.subject: problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
messages.subject_clean: problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
messages.body_plain:
I want to simulate the following (scalar) AR process:

> y_t = 0.3y_{t-1}+0.2_{t-2}+u_t

so I entered the following command in to R:

> VAR.sim(B=matrix(c(0.3,0.2), nrow=1), n=3000, include="none",lag=2)

However, I got the following error message:

>  Error in Bfull[, -c(1, 2)] %*% Yexo : non-conformable arguments
> In addition: Warning messages:
> 1: In cbind(m2[, 1:(i - 1)], matrix(v, nrow = nr), m2[, i:ncol(m2)]) :
>   number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 3)
> 2: In rbind(matrix(0, nrow = p, ncol = k), innov) :
>   number of columns of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 2)

After some debugging, I found the problem is in lines 8-9 of myInsertCol:

>     for (i in c[!c %in% c(1, length(c) + nc)]) m2 <- cbind(m2[,
>         1:(i - 1)], matrix(v, nrow = nr), m2[, i:ncol(m2)])

Before line 8, m2 is [1,1:3] 0 0.3 0.2. However, after line 9, m2 becomes [1,1:3] 0 0 0.3. This is certainly wrong, because one of the coefficient is lost in the process.

What should I do to simulate AR process in tsDyn::VAR.sim. Did I use the function in the wrong way?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Dear Isaac

Thanks you for your message. This is a question that comes up often, but my response is unfortunately not the best: general IRF are not (yet) available in tsDyn. However, if you have a good understranding of them, it should not be too difficult ot generate them, see the FAQ for guidelines:

https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/wiki/FAQ

Best,

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
messages.subject_clean: [tsDyn] problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
messages.body_plain:
Dear Samuel

You can simulate an AR with the VAR function, although the base function arima.sim will be simpler for you.

The problem is that you are not specifying the input matrix correctly: you should give the inputs in the VAR specification, doing as if there were two variables:
library(tsDyn)
B <- matrix(0, nrow=2, ncol=4)
B[1,1] <- 0.3
B[1,3] <- 0.2

VAR.sim(B=B, n=30, include="none",lag=2)

But again, it makes more sense to use arima.sim() for an AR.

best,

Matthieu
